remediation_investigation.tried: Pulled a newer library/postgres:17-alpine (digest sha256:a77aa70e...) and rescanned it with the same Trivy 0.75.0 and live DB.
remediation_investigation.finding: The newer digest fixes krb5-libs (to >=1.22.3-r0) and libxslt (to >=1.1.43-r4): total findings drop from 91 to 62 and both packages disappear.
remediation_investigation.but: security/exceptions.json matches on the full `target` string, which embeds the image digest. Switching compose.yaml to the new digest therefore invalidates all 3 existing postgres exceptions and leaves 26 uncovered HIGH/CRITICAL findings (Go stdlib v1.24.6: 25 HIGH + 1 CRITICAL, from the bundled gosu binary).
remediation_investigation.consequence: Upgrading the digest is NOT a self-contained fix: it requires new, A-approved exceptions bound to the new digest (or replacing gosu), which a developer must not self-approve. Conversely, keeping the current digest keeps the 19 newly-disclosed krb5-libs/libxslt findings uncovered.
remediation_investigation.decision_taken: Do not change compose.yaml and do not add exceptions in this change. Record both states so the owner can decide between (a) upgrade digest + re-approve stdlib exceptions, or (b) keep pin and approve the 19 new advisories with a bound expiry.
remediation_investigation.owner: A (任宇航) for exception approval; B for the digest upgrade and compatibility re-test.
